newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London gave up earlier gains to close lower. December shed $2.20 to close at $320.00, while March closed $1.80 easier at $316.50. In New York raw sugar futures closed a heavily traded session near the day's lows despite early gains, which carried spot-March through resistance at 10.94 cents/lb, and then over the psychologically important level of 11.00 cents/lb. However, in the end March was able to add 5 points to close at 10.86 cents/lb, while May remained flat at 10.81 cents/lb.

As indicated in our first estimate of world sugar production in 1996/97, supplies will be ample this year, which weighs on sentiment. The USDA Attache recently estimated that Indian sugar production in 1996/97 could reach 16.7 million tonnes, raw value, up from a previous estimate of 14.1 million tonnes but down from last year's figure of 18.2 million tonnes. However, in this context it has to be noted that the USDA estimates include khandsari production of around 620,000 tonnes. Brazil is shipping heavily and bagged sugar shipments out of Brazil's port of Paranagua have already exceeded the total exported in 1995.

New business was brisk on the sugar freight market with one route quoted by a charterer for the first time ever, ship brokers said. CSR scored a new first with an inquiry to ship 15,000 tonnes of bulk raw sugar from Queensland to Jeddah for 10-20 November. Saudi Arabia's new refinery in Jeddah is expected to come on stream in early 1997 and should take around 450,000 tonnes of raw sugar for refining throughout the year. Another buyer of raw sugar was apparently China which may have bought between 5 and 10 cargoes of Thai raw sugar over the past few weeks for March/May shipment. Traders in Hong Kong and Bangkok said the Chinese purchases were prompted by low Thai premiums. Traders said the Thai premium, currently quoted at around 75 points for March/May over the New York March futures was at 65 points two weeks earlier. Given current fundamentals, there seems little reason for world prices to go much higher.

EUROPE - Most beet growing areas were dry during the week ended October 15. The harvest progress is steadily improving across the region. In the former Soviet Union, sugar beet areas were dry, which greatly facilitated harvesting operations. Soil moisture levels have declined but are still rated adequate to surplus. Colder air is expected to surge across the area but a prolonged freeze thaw situation, which could spoil beets is not yet indicated.

MEXICO - According to the National Sugar Chamber, Mexico's 1996/97 (November/October) sugar harvest is seen at 4.364 million tonnes, white value, down from the record output of 4.77 million tonnes produced in 1995/96. The lower cane production is ascribed to adverse weather conditions.

CANADA - Sugar imports in July 1996 amounted to 96,891 tonnes, raw value, sharply up on last year's 50,620 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first ten months of 1995/96 (October/July) up to 940,871 tonnes against 848,502 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1994/95 amounted to 1.01 million tonnes against 1.21 million tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of origin in October/July 1995/96 were Australia with 543,120 tonnes raws against 459,957 tonnes, Cuba with 144,744 tonnes compared to 113,480 tonnes and Guatemala with 61,417 tonnes against nil. With shipments of 28,995 tonnes against 113,454 tonnes the previous year, the USA continued to be the largest white sugar supplier in October/July 1995/96. Sugar exports in 1995/96 amounted to 19,492 tonnes, down from 40,450 tonnes exported in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1994/95 hit 43,198 tonnes against 50,343 tonnes in 1993/94. Canadian white sugar almost exclusively goes into the United States which took 15,291 tonnes, down from last year's 34,333 tonnes.

GERMANY - Even though the amount of beet processed in the week ended October, 11 was down, sugar production was up due to a greatly improved sugar content. Due to the early start of the campaign in 1996 cumulative beet deliveries at 6.36 million tonnes are still comfortably up on last year's 5.66 million tonnes and also above the 1994/95 result of 5.85 million tonnes. The estimate for total deliveries for 1996/97 stands unchanged at 26.433 million tonnes, up on last year's actual total of 26.049 million tonnes and the 1994/95 result of 24.211 million tonnes. Sugar content (17.76 per cent) is sharply up on last year's 16.45 per cent and also significantly above the 1994 result of 16.42 per cent. Sugar production so far amounted to 909,990 tonnes, raw value, against 720,368 tonnes in 1995/96 and 747,650 tonnes in 1994/95.
